title: Functional Multi-omics of Aging
text:
Currently, we are in a period of history where the number of individuals over the age of 65 is doubling, leading
to an epidemic of chronic multi-morbidities of old age, and creating an urgent need to discover underlying
mechanisms of aging biology that promote disease. “Functional Multi-omics of Aging” is a training program in
basic and translational aging research for pre- and post-doctoral trainees addressing this need. The program's
success over the last 14 years is documented by outstanding publications and successful careers in biomedical
research of former trainees.

title: Harnessing EHR to develop a Florida-based Coalition on Cancer Care Inequities among PHIV (Social Determinants of Health and Quality of Cancer Care in HIV-associated Cancers)
text:
Although cancer is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality among people with HIV (PWH), they are less likely
to receive any treatment compared to their HIV-seronegative counterparts, even after considering important
clinical factors such as cancer type and cancer stage at diagnosis. Despite the documented inequities in general
healthcare access PWH experience, limited prior work has investigated the role of multi-level social factors,
collectively known as social determinants of health (SDoH), that may impact PWH’s receipt of equitable, high-
quality cancer care. Through the present one-year proposal, we set out to develop the necessary infrastructure
to address this gap in scientific knowledge, leveraging a novel electronic health record-based linkage of multiple
health systems throughout Florida called OneFlorida+ (19 million patients) to gain real world insights into the
role SDoH play in cancer treatment receipt among PWH in the US and facilitate the development of future patient
or provider-level interventions tailored to the HIV oncology care context.

title: Prostate cancer risk stratification via computational 3D pathology
text:
Relevance to public health
This project will develop a nondestructive assay for prostate cancer prognostication based on quantitative
histomorphometric analysis of 3D pathology datasets of prostate specimens (biopsies and surgical excisions).
This project will demonstrate that computational 3D pathology is superior to computational 2D pathology
(including existing clinical nomograms) for distinguishing between aggressive and indolent prostate cancers,
and therefore has value for guiding treatment decisions by urologists and oncologists.

title: New protein-engineered tools and technologies for identifying, deorphanizing, and targeting shed proteins in cancer
text:
Extracellular proteolysis is a hallmark of cancer and has major functional consequences for remodeling cell
surface proteins including receptor activation and shedding of functional extracellular domains. Here, we will
develop technologies to identify novel shed proteins of cell surface, deorphanize interacting partners of these
shed proteins, and generate proteolysis inhibitors to interrogate specific proteolysis events on the cell surface of
cancer cells. We believe our work will significantly impact the functional understanding of shedding events in
cancer, and identify new biomarkers and immunotherapeutic targets.

title: Elucidating Reward Network Modulation in Medial Forebrain Bundle Deep Brain Stimulation for Treatment Resistant Depression
text:
Treatment resistant depression (TRD), representing up to 30% of major depression diagnoses, is an
incapacitating disability affecting millions worldwide. Deep brain stimulation (DBS) is a promising effective
treatment strategy, however, progress has been limited due to an incomplete understanding of the reward
network effects of chronic stimulation for depression. The work proposed in this study, to perform imaging to
understand the evolution of induced reward network expression changes due to stepwise stimulation amplitude
titration, and to correlate their change with improvement in anhedonia, will identify objective biomarkers that
can be used to ultimately guide programming for optimal reward processing improvement.

title: Project 2: InHANCE: Radiation Associated Dysphagia
text:
Project 2
The incidence of highly curable head and neck cancers is rapidly rising, and radiation treatment is very commonly
given at doses sufficient to cause chronic dysphagia (difficulty swallowing). Swallowing function is a driver of
quality-of-life (QOL) after cancer treatment and may cause death from treatment side effects (pneumonia) even
after cancer is cured. This application seeks to understand how quantitative imaging methods might reduce
dysphagia burden through risk stratification, automated diagnostics, and image-guided de-escalation algorithms.

title: Development and Testing of a Multi-Component Intervention to Support HIV Care Engagement among Patients Receiving Cancer Treatment in Zimbabwe
text: Much of the world’s population live in rural areas, where access to specialty care is limited, resulting in unique barriers to seeking care for comorbid conditions across siloed health systems. This study seeks to develop and test solutions to enable concurrent engagement in HIV and cancer care for people with HIV and cancer in Zimbabwe, who face similar barriers with siloed and dispersed treatment institutions. Lessons learned from this study will provide insight for other populations who face barriers to healthcare engagement across siloed systems with limited specialty care options, including rural US settings.

title: Viral Testing
text:
The primary purpose of the virology testing arm of CPRC-SPF breeding program is to assure that its Indian-
origin rhesus macaque colony, supporting NIH-sponsored research specially on HIV/AIDS, is free of Simian
immunodeficiency virus (SIV), Type D Simian retrovirus (SRV-D), Simian T-lymphotropic virus (STLV-1) and
Herpes B virus. Testing is conducted by using the state of the art methodologies.

title: Deciphering the Molecular Features Underlying LRP1-Mediated Tau Spread
text:
There are currently no effective treatments for tauopathies, such as Alzheimer’s Disease (AD). Uptake and
spreading of pathogenic tau is recognized as a key driver of AD pathology, and is primarily mediated by tau's
interaction with the cellular receptor LRP1. Molecular dissection of the tau-LRP1 interaction will enable us to
devise new therapies for AD.

title: Developing MRI Biomarkers of Myelin and Iron in Veterans with Traumatic Brain Injury
text:
The goal of this study is to validate a 3D Short TR Adiabatic Inversion Recovery UTE (STAIR-UTE) sequence
for myelin imaging, and a 3D UTE quantitative susceptibility mapping (3D UTE-QSM) technique for iron imaging,
then characterize longitudinal changes in demyelination and iron accumulation in brains of mice subjected to
open-field low-intensity blast (LIB), and finally apply the 3D STAIR-UTE and UTE-QSM techniques to evaluate
cross-sectional changes in demyelination and iron accumulation in two groups of Veterans, one group with
history of mTBI and the other group with no history of mTBI.

title: Striatal Regulation of Prefrontal Cortical Circuit Maturation:  Mechanisms and Implications for ASD
text:
The dorsomedial prefrontal cortex (dmPFC) and the striatum are interconnected through recurrent cortico-basal
ganglia-thalamocortical loops that support a wide range of cognitive, affective, and motor functions. While the
influence of cortical activity on striatal development is well recognized, the reciprocal impact of striatal activity on
cortical maturation remains poorly understood. This proposal investigates how imbalances in postnatal striatal
output affect the development of prefrontal circuits, with a focus on the activity-dependent maturation of cortical
interneurons. We will further examine the relevance of this mechanism in a genetic mouse model of autism
spectrum disorder (Shank3B). By uncovering how striatal dysfunction disrupts cortical circuit formation, this work
will provide critical insight into the pathogenesis of neurodevelopmental disorders involving frontostriatal
dysfunction and may reveal novel targets for early therapeutic intervention.

title: Optimizing gamma-delta T cell receptor-mediated signaling to improve cancer immunotherapy
text:
gd T cells, a subset of whole T cell population, can initiate tumor killing by detecting cancer antigens (some
metabolites or small fragments of cancer proteins) through their cell surface gd T cell receptor (TCR)-CD3 protein
complexes. One type of immunotherapy that involves altering gdTCR-CD3 mediated signaling can help the
immune system to fight against deadly cancers. This proposal aims to identify and alter the critical amino acids
(small molecules that constitute a protein) on the gdTCR that are involved in CD3-mediated signaling, leading to
enhanced tumor killing by gd T cells as a means of devising new strategies for cancer immunotherapy.

title: Intestinal chondroitin sulfate glycosaminoglycans and their role in inflammatory bowel disease
text:
The worldwide prevalence of inflammatory bowel disease and its associated economic burden continue to rise.
Increasing evidence implicates impaired extracellular matrix function in the pathogenesis of inflammatory bowel
disease, but studies testing the role of extracellular matrix augmentation as therapy for inflammatory bowel
disease or as a biomarker are limited. The goal of this work is to investigate whether chondroitin sulfate
glycosaminoglycan elements in the intestinal extracellular matrix can be used as novel therapeutic agents in
inflammatory bowel disease and whether their composition at diagnosis can predict clinical disease outcomes.

title: The Role of Ischemia Reperfusion Injury in Lung Allograft Rejection
text:
Lung transplantation is an established therapy for many patients who suffer from end stage
pulmonary failure. Current treatment strategies for lung transplant recipients, which rely on
targeting adaptive immune cells in the recipient, have many side effects and are only modestly
effective as many lungs ultimately fail due to graft rejection. In this grant application we propose
to study alternative approaches which are based on targeting innate immune pathways that are
activated immediately after reperfusion of the transplanted lung and augment alloimmune
responses.

title: The Cancer Cell Map Initiative v2.0
text:
THE CANCER CELL MAP INITIATIVE v2.0
OVERALL NARRATIVE
Although much attention has been devoted to mapping the tumor genome, understanding cancer requires that
we move beyond simply cataloguing the genes associated with it. It is critical to understand the many interactions
among these genes and the corresponding proteins, and how these complex networks give rise to tumor
initiation, progression and metastasis. The Cancer Cell Map Initiative (CCMI) is applying systematic approaches
to comprehensively map the molecular networks that underlie cancer and to use these maps as key resources
for precision medicine.

title: The Role of SMARCAL1 Depletion on Increased Immunogenicity in ALT+ Gliomas
text:
PROJECT NARRATIVE.
SMARCAL1 is a novel tumor specific therapeutic target for high grade gliomas (HGGs) that utilize alternative
lengthening of telomeres (ALT). We will investigate the effects of targeting SMARCAL1 on inflammation
within tumor cells and the ability of immune cells to recognize and respond. These studies will provide novel
insight into the mechanisms governing tumor-intrinsic inflammatory signaling and how they can be targeted
for glioma immunotherapy.

title: University of Pennsylvania Patient-derived Xenograft Development and Trials Center
text:
University of Pennsylvania PDX Development and Trial Centers Project Narrative –
Human malignancies, particularly AML and ovarian, continue to have a high mortality. We will optimize human
patient derived xenotransplantation models for AML, ovarian cancer and other malignancies and use these
models to test new therapies for these diseases.

title: Wnt-Retinoic Acid Regulation of Gastric Epithelial Cells
text:
This project will define basic mechanisms of stomach tissue maintenance and uncover molecular pathways
that are important for cellular repair after tissue injury. The findings will advance knowledge of gastric stem cell
biology, which is important to refine strategies to propagate adult stem cells in culture for regenerative
therapies and to develop potential therapies for gastric hyperproliferative diseases.

title: Mechanotransducive role of muscle progenitors and bone formation in fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva
text:
Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva (FOP) is a debilitating human genetic disorder of
progressive bone growth within skeletal muscles and hence all current interventions aim
to reduce bone formation. Here, we propose that FOP is not only a disease of ectopic
bone formation, but also impaired skeletal muscle regeneration, and we provide a strategy
to gain unique insight into fundamental mechanisms regulate tissue homeostasis and
repair. The studies present here will investigate previously undefined cellular extensions
by which adult progenitor cells interact to sense their microenvironment, investigate how
the mechanosensory protein Piezo1 regulates function in fibroadipogenic progenitors, and
test a potential pharmacological intervention to boostregeneration and diminish aberrant
bonein diseased tissues.
